back: It checks each element in turn from the start until it finds the target or reaches the end. Works on unsorted data; $O(n)$.
On a sorted list, compare the target with the middle element and discard the half that can’t contain it; repeat. $O(\log n)$.

front: What does Big O notation describe?
back: How an algorithm’s running time (or memory) grows as the input size grows, usually in the worst case.
